text: As I have mentioned, this is not entirely new, it is similar to the obligations under the Smoking (Prohibition in Certain Places) Act that public entertainment premises are already subject to and it is not meant to be onerous or impose a disproportionate amount of legal liability on premise operators.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: HSA will support them in complying with these obligations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Practical guidance on the identification of prohibited products, how to engage and handle individuals possessing or using these prohibited products and when to engage HSA for further assistance, will be provided.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To protect these owners and occupiers, it will be an offence for individuals to hinder, obstruct, threaten, abuse or assault owners and occupiers in the course of performing their duties.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yip asked about the safeguards that ensure the accuracy of our laboratory tests, given that a positive urine test can be presumed to mean that the individual has consumed SPS and committed an offence.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: HSA has extensive experience supporting CNB in conducting laboratory tests for enforcement under the MDA.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, these powers and capabilities are not new to HSA.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Expanded powers require adequate resources to support implementation – this was also a point emphasised by a few Members.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We adopted a whole-of-Government enforcement approach, where relevant agencies, such as the Police, CNB, NEA and National Parks Board (NParks) assist in the detection and referral of suspected cases to HSA.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These agencies will continue to be authorised under the TVCA.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To Mr Yip's question, HSA carefully assesses the suitability of these officers before empowering them with enforcement powers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This applies to officers from HSA and across other agencies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Officers are only authorised for specific powers that match their roles and experience and must also undergo prescribed training and competency assessments before being deployed.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: After deployment, they continue to be overseen and reviewed by their supervisors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On rehabilitation capacity, having operated these programmes for the past six months, we have provided for sufficient capacity, including in the DRC.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will regularly review capacity utilisation and projections, based on the latest offender numbers and trends and make the necessary adjustments.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Beyond the number of offenders, we also monitor recidivism rates and other key indicators.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: MHA already works with international and regional partners, such as the Commission on Narcotic Drugs, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime and the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (ASEAN) counterparts, to monitor the emergence of new psychoactive substances.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: MOH and MHA also review various sources of data to identify and be alert to emerging substances of abuse.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Specific to vaporisers, HSA also collects and exchanges intelligence with the World Health Organization and international regulatory counterparts and, on our own, we conduct random testing of vaporisers that we have seized to detect any new substances that is emerging in our market.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, there will be less scrambling and a lot more responsiveness to any emerging threats.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Gerald Giam cited clause 37 on the definition of smoking.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is not for the Tobacco Control Act, but it is actually an amendment to NEA's Smoking (Prohibition in Certain Places) Act.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Smoking Area Ban policy is also under MSE and NEA's purview, but I understand where the Member is coming from.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will work with NEA and MSE on the Member of Parliament's suggestion to see how we can continue to help manage the issue of second-hand smoke and smoking within our heartlands.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On the suggestion to reduce addictiveness or tobacco and nicotine products, the Member of Parliament was likely referring to the nicotine cap policy I had mentioned earlier.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We have considered this before and will continue to study it.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, our limits are no different from what the Member has cited from the UK.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Are there any clarifications arising out of Senior Minister of State Koh's response?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: If not, I will put the question to the House.      .
